title: Kalshi moves into a new kind of gambling: the stock market
summary:
Everything is gambling now: the latest news on prediction markets like Polymarket and KalshiKalshi is getting ready to offer stock trading on its platform, according to reports from The Wall Street Journal and CNBC.
The company reportedly plans to use its acquisition of broker FB Securities to launch equities and exchange-traded funds “within the next two months,” pitting the prediction market against rivals like Robinhood.
The rumored expansion into stock trading comes as Kalshi faces a growing number of legal battles over its prediction market platform across the US.
At the same time, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission is pushing back on state efforts to regulate prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket, arguing that it has the “exclusive” authority over them.
Nine Democratic senators wrote a letter to the CFTC this week, urging it to stop interfering with state bans on prediction markets.

title: Andy Burnham promises to 'move quickly' on Neets report
summary:
The prime minister has said he wants to "move quickly" on implementing recommendations in Alan Milburn's report on work and young people.
Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Andy Burnham said: "This isn't about waiting forever and a long-off-promised reform, I want to get stuck into it right now."
Milburn's report, external urged more job support for under-25s, a shake-up of the benefits system, early intervention in schools and tax cuts for businesses hiring young people.
Burnham praised the report as a "landmark moment" adding: "This is not just a benefits reform, it's a whole society change he is calling for."
He said he wanted 45-day work placements offered to every 16-18-year-old "who wants one" and was working on funding the places.

title: What’s holding South Africa’s economy back?
summary:
South Africa seeks billions in new investment to revive weak growth and tackle unemployment crisis.
And last year, more foreign investment left South Africa than came in.
President Cyril Ramaphosa is courting US tech giants to help make South Africa an AI hub.
But Washington has hit South Africa with steep tariffs and is cutting its duty-free access to the US market.
So, can South Africa win back investors and turn promises into jobs?

title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?
summary:
Nvidia and its co-founder Jensen Huang have been at the centre of the artificial intelligence (AI) spending boom.
The billions of dollars being funnelled into AI and the construction of data centres has bolstered the American economy, with Nvidia being one of the biggest spenders.
Huang played a major role in the company, leading its shift towards AI, and maintained a firm grip on the company, with up to 200 people directly reporting to him.
Such a move could spell a wider slowdown in AI investment, which would have an economic impact.
Kunjan Sobhani, senior technology industry analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, expects the impact of Huang leaving to be "limited" for now as Nvidia has strong commitments and a deep order book.

title: Want VC Funding? Here Are 6 Ways to Stand Out.
summary:
Approach the right investors (not every investor), and make investors believe you can execute without them.
From an investor’s perspective, originality and market potential matter, but they’re rarely enough to justify an investment.
Others came from less polished founders with limited resources but a better understanding of how to build a sustainable business.
Founders need to ask themselves a simple question: Why should an investor believe I’m capable of building the business I’m describing?
Now the founder needs more capital, and new investors aren’t willing to pay what previous investors paid.

title: Russia's Energy Crisis so Bad It Looks to Imports and Low-Quality Fuel
summary:
The crisis has been months in the making, as Kyiv wages a long-range strike campaign pummeling Russian energy facilities, claiming this week to have knocked out about 55% of total refinery capacity so far.
Alexander Novak, a deputy prime minister and Russia's senior official overseeing energy, was cited telling his subordinates to prioritize expanding petrol imports and "securing additional volumes of out-of-class fuel."
London-based shipping analytics firm Vortexa separately put Russia's August fuel imports at about 470,000 metric tons.
But those imports took place over entire years, while GUR's estimate of nearly 1 million metric tons in imports covers just four months.
Novak's office and the Russian energy ministry did not immediately respond to comment requests sent outside regular business hours by Business Insider.

title: Defeating Volatility: Market wealth at 10-month peak on peppy sentiment
summary:
SynopsisIndia's global market capitalisation has seen a remarkable upswing since October, adding about $500 billion and reaching close to $5.42 trillion.
This rebound has enabled India to reclaim its fifth-place ranking in the world.
The return of foreign investors, after a substantial sell-off in AI stocks, is a testament to India's recovery against the backdrop of ongoing economic and market turbulence.
